newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: EU/S.Africa trade talks resume in Pretoria Jan 24.
newsitem.headline: EU/S.Africa trade talks resume in Pretoria Jan 24.

text.p: The South African government said on Tuesday that stalled trade negotiations with the European Union would resume in Pretoria on January 24.
The Department of Trade and Industry said in a statement that South Africa would outline its negotiating mandate at the long-awaited meeting.

"At this meeting the South African government will present a document outlining its position on a long term agreement on trade and economic cooperation and it will form a basis for discussions with the EU," the department said.

The South African negotiating team would be headed by the country's ambassador to the EU and include senior officials from the departments of trade and industry, foreign affairs, agriculture and finance.
South Africa had said it wanted a speedy resumption of the talks after it broke an impasse last month when it made know its negotiating mandate to the EU.
The EU, which absorbs some 40 percent of South African exports and accounts for more than a third of South African imports, set out its negotiating mandate in March last year.
